content.value: (B) COLLAPSED IDENTITY — gr-bl-peer-ip-container. The containerized control plane's Caddy hop arrives from the docker bridge gateway (172.18.0.1), and trust_forwarded_ip (router.ex:367) only calls RemoteIp when loopback_peer?(conn.remote_ip) is true — so it silently no-ops. TWO defects in one row, and the second is the serious one: every session row renders uniform garbage in the account UI, AND the device-auth `start:<ip>` rate bucket collapses to ONE GLOBAL BUCKET shared by every user, so a single abusive client throttles the entire platform. The fix must widen the trusted-peer predicate to the container gateway WITHOUT ever trusting an attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-For from a non-proxy peer — the existing comment at router.ex:365 states that invariant and it must survive.

content.value: 2. THE REFETCH STORM IS FULLY DE-RISKED, AND NARROWER THAN THE DIRECTION GUESSED. It is neither a blanket refetch nor N independent subscribers. TYPE_ACTIONS (app.js:12018-12061) is a closed, view-conditional dispatch table that behaves correctly for most event types. Exactly FOUR types — fleet, onboarding, barkpark.suspended, barkpark.restored — funnel through invalidateFleet (11970) and invalidateOnboarding (11995) into ONE shared monolith, loadOverview() (4847-4921), which unconditionally issues all five GETs on every call with zero awareness of which collection actually changed. There is no debounce, no dedupe, no in-flight guard, no AbortController anywhere in the 17k-line file. Cold boot calls loadOverview() exactly once (5 requests); seven SSE ticks add 35; total 40 — the production measurement, reproduced from code alone. Because the repeats are EVENLY SPACED, a time-window debounce would not suppress them: the fix must be scope-narrowing, not throttling. Falsifiable deterministically by a synthetic-event test counting fetch calls per type — no production access required. The second attack on this direction ('your flagship fix may be unfalsifiable') is answered.

content.value: CORRECTION 1 — THE SSE TICKET IS NOT FREE, AND THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT NEW FACT. The direction named the constraint 'EventSource cannot set headers, so a header is NOT the fix — mint a short-TTL single-use SSE-scoped ticket.' The first half is right. The second half hides an architectural tension the survey exposed: EventSource freezes its URL at construction (app.js:11919), and the client's onerror handler (11943-11954) only toasts and repaints the liveness chip — it never closes or reopens the stream. Native browser reconnect therefore replays the SAME frozen URL forever. A literal single-use ticket means the first connection consumes it and EVERY subsequent native retry 401s permanently — a regression strictly worse than the leak being fixed, and it would fail the task's own criterion 2 on any network flap. There are exactly two honest resolutions: (a) ship short-TTL MULTI-connect and name it that, never overselling it as single-use; or (b) ship true single-use AND rewrite the client reconnect path — close, mint over a bearer header, reconstruct EventSource, add explicit backoff to avoid a mint storm, and extend the liveness state machine to model an app-driven remint gap. This is a DECIDE-TIME RULING, not a builder detail. The mechanism itself needs no migration: user_tokens.context is an unconstrained string column, 2fa_pending is the short-TTL mint template, and reset_password_by_token is the battle-tested single-use consume-in-transaction template.

CORRECTION 1 — THE SSE TICKET IS NOT FREE, AND THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT NEW FACT. The direction named the constraint 'EventSource cannot set headers, so a header is NOT the fix — mint a short-TTL single-use SSE-scoped ticket.' The first half is right. The second half hides an architectural tension the survey exposed: EventSource freezes its URL at construction (app.js:11919), and the client's onerror handler (11943-11954) only toasts and repaints the liveness chip — it never closes or reopens the stream. Native browser reconnect therefore replays the SAME frozen URL forever. A literal single-use ticket means the first connection consumes it and EVERY subsequent native retry 401s permanently — a regression strictly worse than the leak being fixed, and it would fail the task's own criterion 2 on any network flap. There are exactly two honest resolutions: (a) ship short-TTL MULTI-connect and name it that, never overselling it as single-use; or (b) ship true single-use AND rewrite the client reconnect path — close, mint over a bearer header, reconstruct EventSource, add explicit backoff to avoid a mint storm, and extend the liveness state machine to model an app-driven remint gap. This is a DECIDE-TIME RULING, not a builder detail. The mechanism itself needs no migration: user_tokens.context is an unconstrained string column, 2fa_pending is the short-TTL mint template, and reset_password_by_token is the battle-tested single-use consume-in-transaction template.
